## L1 Capability: Identity and Access Management

Identity and Access Management is the enterprise security capability that establishes and governs the digital identities of all subjects — human users, non-human systems, and AI agents — and controls their access to enterprise resources through verified authentication, explicit authorization, and continuous monitoring. As the architectural control plane for Zero Trust, IAM is a cross-cutting capability consumed by every application, platform, and infrastructure domain. It interfaces with adjacent security capabilities (endpoint security, network security, data security, security operations) to provide identity context as a shared input to access decisions across the enterprise.

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity Indicator |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity Lifecycle Management** | Provisioning, modification, and deprovisioning of digital identities across all populations (workforce, partner, customer, non-human) in alignment with joiner-mover-leaver processes | Defined |
| **Identity Governance and Administration (IGA)** | Access review, entitlement management, role lifecycle management, separation of duties enforcement, and certification campaigns ensuring access remains appropriate over time | Developing |
| **Authentication** | Verification of claimed identity through multi-factor, phishing-resistant, and federated authentication mechanisms aligned to NIST SP 800-63B Authenticator Assurance Levels | Defined |
| **Authorization** | Policy-based access control (RBAC, ABAC) and real-time policy decision and enforcement that governs what authenticated identities may do, on what resources, and under what conditions | Developing |
| **Identity Federation and Single Sign-On** | Establishment and governance of trust relationships between identity domains, enabling authenticated identity claims to flow across organizational and technical boundaries without redundant authentication | Defined |
| **Credential and Attribute Management** | Lifecycle management of credentials (passwords, certificates, tokens, API keys) and identity attributes that express entitlement and context, including rotation, revocation, and secure storage | Defined |
| **Privileged Access Management** | Control of elevated and administrative access through credential vaulting, just-in-time access, session management, tiered administration models, and least-privilege enforcement for privileged identities | Defined |
| **Identity Proofing and Assurance** | Evidence-based verification of identity claims at enrollment, establishing the IAL (Identity Assurance Level) against which subsequent authentication and access decisions are calibrated | Developing |
| **Non-Human and AI Identity Management** | Governance of service accounts, workload identities, API clients, and AI/ML system identities through cryptographic binding, short-lived credentials, and behavioral monitoring | Initial |
| **Identity Monitoring and Analytics** | Continuous logging, behavioral baseline establishment, anomaly detection, and threat correlation for identity-related events across all identity populations | Developing |

## Scope and Boundaries

**In Scope**: Management of digital identities and access across all identity populations and access patterns; authentication, authorization, and governance outcomes; identity data flows between IAM capabilities and consuming applications; identity proofing and assurance lifecycle

**Out of Scope**:

- Network segmentation and perimeter controls (see Network Security capability map)
- Endpoint device trust management and device posture beyond its use as an authentication signal (see Endpoint Security capability map)
- Data classification, labeling, and data loss prevention (see Information Security capability map)
- Physical access control and facility identity management
- Security operations and incident response beyond identity-event detection (see SecOps capability map)

**Non-ABB Guardrail**: This document defines capabilities at L1/L2 only. Architecture Building Blocks, solution patterns, security controls, vendor selections, and compliance requirements are explicitly out of scope for this artifact.
